raw_findings.body: The returned set contains the literal string "Clients" instead of client UUIDs; consumers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource do `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()` and dereference null, producing a NullPointerException / 500. Additionally, per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource have no resource type set, so they are never matched by findByType and genuinely granted clients are omitted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Method returns a set that mixes/omits identifiers, breaking the documented contract that the set contains client ids.
raw_findings.impact: The returned set contains the literal string "Clients" instead of client UUIDs; consumers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource do `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()` and dereference null, producing a NullPointerException / 500. Additionally, per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource have no resource type set, so they are never matched by findByType and genuinely granted clients are omitted.
raw_findings.root_cause: The V2 override reuses findByType with the schema resource-type name, but in the V2 schema the type-level resource itself carries that type while per-client resources carry no type at all, so the filter selects exactly the wrong resources.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Skip the resource whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and enumerate the actual per-client resources (e.g. iterate realm clients and call hasPermission(client, scope), or set the resource type when creating per-client resources).
raw_findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the "Clients" resource-type resource name instead of client ids
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator is granted a scope on the schema-level "Clients" resource (the all-clients resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name and type both equal to "Clients"), and a caller invokes ClientPermissionEvaluator#getClientsWithPermission (e.g. AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions).

raw_findings.body: canManageClientScopes() returns true while canViewClientScopes() (which delegates to canView()) returns false, so the same admin can modify client scopes but receives 403 Forbidden when listing/viewing them.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent authorization decisions between manage and view checks for the same principal.
raw_findings.impact: canManageClientScopes() returns true while canViewClientScopes() (which delegates to canView()) returns false, so the same admin can modify client scopes but receives 403 Forbidden when listing/viewing them.
raw_findings.root_cause: canView() only consults the VIEW scope, whereas the sibling overrides (canManageClientScopes, canView(ClientScopeModel)) treat MANAGE as implying view, breaking the manage-implies-view invariant of the V1 implementation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make canView() also return true when hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is true (or when canManage() is true).
raw_findings.title: canView() ignores the all-clients MANAGE permission, so manage-capable admins cannot view client scopes
raw_findings.trigger: An admin without MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS roles is granted only the all-clients MANAGE permission (as in testManageAllClients) and calls an endpoint gated by requireViewClientScopes()/requireView(), e.g. GET /admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes.

raw_findings.body: Instead of a permission denial (HTTP 403), the request fails with an unchecked UnsupportedOperationException resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error for token exchange.
raw_findings.evidence:
public boolean canExchangeTo(ClientModel authorizedClient, ClientModel to, AccessToken token) {
        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime exception escapes to the token endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: Instead of a permission denial (HTTP 403), the request fails with an unchecked UnsupportedOperationException resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error for token exchange.
raw_findings.root_cause: A method that is still invoked from a non-admin runtime code path (token exchange) was overridden to throw rather than to return false when V2 does not model exchange permissions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return false (deny) from canExchangeTo in V2, or feature-gate the AbstractTokenExchangeProvider call so it is not reached when FGAP V2 is active.
raw_findings.title: canExchangeTo override throws UnsupportedOperationException on a runtime token-exchange path
raw_findings.trigger: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled together with the (independent) token-exchange feature and a client performs a token exchange targeting another client; AbstractTokenExchangeProvider:276 calls AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token).

validated_findings.body: The returned set contains the literal string "Clients" instead of client UUIDs; consumers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource do `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()` and dereference null, producing a NullPointerException / 500. Additionally, per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource have no resource type set, so they are never matched by findByType and genuinely granted clients are omitted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Method returns a set that mixes/omits identifiers, breaking the documented contract that the set contains client ids.
validated_findings.impact: The returned set contains the literal string "Clients" instead of client UUIDs; consumers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource do `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()` and dereference null, producing a NullPointerException / 500. Additionally, per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource have no resource type set, so they are never matched by findByType and genuinely granted clients are omitted.
validated_findings.root_cause: The V2 override reuses findByType with the schema resource-type name, but in the V2 schema the type-level resource itself carries that type while per-client resources carry no type at all, so the filter selects exactly the wrong resources.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Skip the resource whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and enumerate the actual per-client resources (e.g. iterate realm clients and call hasPermission(client, scope), or set the resource type when creating per-client resources).
validated_findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the "Clients" resource-type resource name instead of client ids
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator is granted a scope on the schema-level "Clients" resource (the all-clients resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name and type both equal to "Clients"), and a caller invokes ClientPermissionEvaluator#getClientsWithPermission (e.g. AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that per-client resources have no type set is speculative. AdminPermissionsSchema.init creates type-level resources with type set, and getOrCreateResource for individual clients also sets the type. The patch shows findByType with CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE which matches the schema initialization. No concrete evidence that the wrong resources are selected.

validated_findings.body: canManageClientScopes() returns true while canViewClientScopes() (which delegates to canView()) returns false, so the same admin can modify client scopes but receives 403 Forbidden when listing/viewing them.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent authorization decisions between manage and view checks for the same principal.
validated_findings.impact: canManageClientScopes() returns true while canViewClientScopes() (which delegates to canView()) returns false, so the same admin can modify client scopes but receives 403 Forbidden when listing/viewing them.
validated_findings.root_cause: canView() only consults the VIEW scope, whereas the sibling overrides (canManageClientScopes, canView(ClientScopeModel)) treat MANAGE as implying view, breaking the manage-implies-view invariant of the V1 implementation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make canView() also return true when hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is true (or when canManage() is true).
validated_findings.title: canView() ignores the all-clients MANAGE permission, so manage-capable admins cannot view client scopes
validated_findings.trigger: An admin without MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS roles is granted only the all-clients MANAGE permission (as in testManageAllClients) and calls an endpoint gated by requireViewClientScopes()/requireView(), e.g. GET /admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that canManageClientScopes implies view but canView does not check MANAGE is speculative. Looking at the V1 base class, canView() returns canManageClientsDefault() || canViewClientDefault(), and canManageClientScopes() returns canManageClientsDefault(). The V2 canView() adds hasPermission(MANAGE) check is not shown but the claim about inconsistency is not proven from the patch.

validated_findings.body: Instead of a permission denial (HTTP 403), the request fails with an unchecked UnsupportedOperationException resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error for token exchange.
validated_findings.evidence:
public boolean canExchangeTo(ClientModel authorizedClient, ClientModel to, AccessToken token) {
        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2");
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime exception escapes to the token endpoint.
validated_findings.impact: Instead of a permission denial (HTTP 403), the request fails with an unchecked UnsupportedOperationException resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error for token exchange.
validated_findings.root_cause: A method that is still invoked from a non-admin runtime code path (token exchange) was overridden to throw rather than to return false when V2 does not model exchange permissions.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Return false (deny) from canExchangeTo in V2, or feature-gate the AbstractTokenExchangeProvider call so it is not reached when FGAP V2 is active.
validated_findings.title: canExchangeTo override throws UnsupportedOperationException on a runtime token-exchange path
validated_findings.trigger: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled together with the (independent) token-exchange feature and a client performs a token exchange targeting another client; AbstractTokenExchangeProvider:276 calls AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that token exchange calls canExchangeTo in V2 is speculative. The search shows TOKEN_EXCHANGE features depend on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), not V2. The comment in Profile.java shows TOKEN_EXCHANGE_STANDARD_V2 depends on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, not ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. No evidence this code path is reached when V2 is active.
